dataset_family: Chosun University Hospital, Gwangju (South Korea): 75 MCI recruited from the community and the hospital Dementia Clinic, Apr 2017 to Jan 2021 (17 AD converters / 58 non-converters), mean follow-up 24 months; not a public dataset
method_family: Evidence type for VF-27: a baseline continuous GDS score compared between AD converters and non-converters (unpaired t-test) in a small longitudinal memory-clinic/community prognosis cohort. The paper's primary method is serial florbetaben amyloid-PET SUVR with Cox and ROC. At the evidence level it is the same kind of analysis as P-647's Table 4 (a baseline depression scale in converters vs non-converters)
what_it_shows: Baseline GDS was the same in the 17 MCI patients who converted to AD and the 58 who did not (10.1 +/- 7.7 vs 9.7 +/- 7.3, unpaired t-test p = 0.850), and the authors list GDS among the baseline variables that did not differ. GDS was not entered into the Cox models and was never related to amyloid burden. All participants have MCI.
why: Choo et al., Psychiatry Investig 2022;19(5):394-400. The PDF title, DOI and the Chosun/Gwangju cohort match the summaries.md block and the map entry. The block never mentions GDS; the evidence is in the PDF. Against the Table A1 statement it supports the conversion limb of the severity clause: in the study's own converter-versus-non-converter comparison, a continuous depression score did not separate the groups. This is the same kind of result round 20 accepted from P-647's Table 4, so it is marked 'yes' on the same standard. What it does NOT show: the first clause (all participants have MCI); the brain-measures limb (amyloid PET was acquired, but GDS was never correlated with SUVR or any imaging measure); the 'although' clause. Limits: 17 converters, so the null is low-powered; the only analysis is a descriptive t-test, and GDS is absent from the adjusted Cox models; the GDS version is not stated (the means and SDs suggest the 30-item form, but that is an inference); people with current serious psychiatric disorders affecting cognition, and anyone on psychoactive medication, were excluded, so antidepressant-treated depression is absent and the range may be somewhat restricted, although the SD of about 7.5 shows substantial spread; the outcome is AD conversion only. Independence: no shared sample, site or authors with P-643, although both are Korean single-centre clinical cohorts: P-643 is Korea University Guro in Seoul, P-974 is Chosun University in Gwangju, and the author lists do not overlap (Hoowon Kim of Chosun is not Junhyung Kim of Korea University Guro). None with P-647 or with the other candidates. Method-family caution: as with P-647, the depression evidence is a baseline-scale converter comparison.

quotes.quote: Seventy-five individuals with MCI were recruited from the community and from the Dementia Clinic, Chosun University Hospital, Gwangju, South Korea from April 2017 to January 2021.

The exclusion criteria included any current serious medical, psychiatric, or neurological disorder affecting the patient's cognitive function, evidence of focal brain lesions on MRI including multiple lacunes and white matter hyperintensities (WMH) of grade 2 or more on the Fazekas scale;12 presence of severe behavioral or communication difficulties; or a current use of psychoactive medication.
Demographic and clinical data from the two groups (converter and non-converter) were compared using an unpaired t-test, while the χ2 test was applied to compare proportions and categorical data.
Of the 75 MCI participants, 17 (22.7% total, or an annual rate of 11.4%) converted to AD.

*significant at p<0.05 for unpaired T or chi-square tests. CDR, Clinical Dementia Rating; SMC, Subjective Memory Complaints; GDS, Geriatric Depression Scale

MCI converters did not show statistically significant differences in terms of age, education, mean cortical amyloid burden, CDR, Subjective Memory Complaints, Geriatric Depression Scale, and APOE ε4 allele ratios, compared to MCI non-converters.
